fatal_errors: The claimed 56.96% hardness increase is arithmetically inconsistent with the cited values of 460.1 and 535.8 Hv; those values represent an increase of about 16.5%.
The proposed experiment lists no hardness measurement even though increased hardness is a central prediction and part of the falsification rule.
explanation: This is not a reconstruction of the target CoCrFeNiTi high-energy-ball-milling/SPS treatment, processing window, nanocrystalline FCC/BCC mediator, or reported properties. It is nevertheless a relevant alternative hypothesis: Cr addition to HfMoTaTiZr is associated with measurable strength and fracture-strain improvements, and the cited paper supports Cr-induced solid-solution strengthening and formation of a reticulated Laves phase. Evidence discipline is weakened by the erroneous hardness percentage, reliance on three summaries of the same paper, and presentation of some mechanistic interpretation as established. The baseline is clear, but the boundary statement does not identify useful composition, processing, Laves-fraction, or temperature limits. The controlled comparison could falsify the broad property claim, but it needs hardness testing, matched processing, replication and uncertainty criteria, and preferably the same mechanical test mode used by the supporting study.
